title: Chapter Dependency Map
question: How do chapter links connect the physical machine to its operational release?
scope: The rendered legend weights links by counts labeled citations and marks a dashed Light link; these are chapter relationships, not runtime causality or mandatory completion tracking.

steps.title: Read what the arrows encode
steps.description: The printed legend distinguishes link weights labeled 5 to 9 citations, 10 to 19, and 20 or more, plus a dashed Light link. Line weight expresses the mapped chapter-reference relationship; it is not execution speed or physical authority.

steps.title: Establish the physical foundation
steps.description: The Causal Boundary introduces the machine model. Body, Brain, and Nervous System develop the physical and computational responsibilities that later chapters build on.

steps.title: Connect learning to evaluation
steps.description: Physical Data feeds Policy Training, which feeds Closed-Loop Evaluation. The sequence connects the conditions recorded in data to evidence about the resulting policy.

steps.title: Follow the runtime chain
steps.description: Sensor Perception, Spatial Memory, Grounded Intent, and Trajectory Planning lead toward Safety Enforcement and Workload Placement. These chapter links organize learning prerequisites rather than depict packets or admitted commands moving through hardware.

steps.title: Connect operation to accountable release
steps.description: Supervisory Intervention and Adversarial Verification support Deployment Release. Both intervention and release connect to Responsible Physical AI, so operational authority requires more than a trained model.

steps.title: Transfer the method
steps.description: Engineering Physical AI closes the map by synthesizing the preceding responsibilities and transferring the method to unfamiliar machines. The map guides reading; it does not require a software-style completion state.

review_notes: Fresh canonical chapter SVG and corrected caption inspected. Solid weights encode the visible citation-count bands and dashed arrows are light links. Chapter regions and legend retain the original geometry.

title: One permission tick
question: Why is an unloaded execution time insufficient to justify the permission schedule?
scope: The unloaded run is an illustrative observation, not a measurement. The declared WCET is a bound requiring analysis, and deadline and period are different constraints.

wcet.label: Declared WCET and hatched justification gap

steps.title: Locate the release and next release
steps.description: The period spans one release to the next. It does not mean this permission job may consume the entire period.

steps.title: Separate observation from a bound
steps.description: The unloaded bar reports only the illustrative run. The hatched extension to declared WCET is work the timing analysis must justify under permitted conditions.

steps.title: Charge blocking and interference to slack
steps.description: The job must finish by the deadline, before the next release. Slack between WCET and deadline is the available room for blocking and interference.

steps.title: Translate time into motion
steps.description: The lower axis shows the base’s travel over the same tick. Time spent waiting or executing is also time in which the machine continues moving.

title: The two-processor implementation
question: How does a learned proposal reach the drives without giving the application processor drive authority?
scope: The processors share no memory. This architecture does not by itself establish a certified safety function.

steps.title: Produce a proposal
steps.description: Perception conditions the intent model and chunk policy. The application processor proposes motion but has no access to drive registers.

steps.title: Cross a checked link
steps.description: Framed packets cross the SPI or CAN FD board link with CRC and sequence information. The receive path places checked proposals in the microcontroller’s own memory.

steps.title: Admit against current state
steps.description: The permission tick checks freshness, lease, and limits against measured state. Only an admitted command proceeds to the drives.

steps.title: Close the physical loop
steps.description: Drives close current and velocity loops and move the plant. Encoders and scanner return measured state to permission checking and telemetry to perception.

title: Hardware proposal boundary
question: What changes when the learned host can write the drive registers directly?
scope: The two panels compare authority and failure containment; neither panel alone certifies a safety integrity level.

steps.title: Keep proposal separate
steps.description: In panel (a), the application processor sends a proposal across a checked board link. It cannot directly write the drive registers.

steps.title: Give permission its own domain
steps.description: The safety MCU holds the mailbox in its own memory and checks state, freshness, and lease at the permission tick. It is the sole writer of the drive registers.

steps.title: Retain an inhibit route

steps.title: Inspect the collapsed alternative

title: Illustrative out-of-band interlock and STO path

sto.label: Drive STO inputs and power stage

steps.title: Open both channels

steps.title: Check relay release before restart

steps.title: Remove torque production
steps.description: The two STO inputs disable torque production in the drive. The motor can still coast after torque is removed.

steps.title: Distinguish the brake circuit

steps.title: Follow learner-induced drift

title: Contact force against brake onset

fastmargin.label: Fast brake onset and remaining margin

guardmargin.label: Guarded brake onset and remaining margin

steps.title: Detect force at the tripwire
steps.description: Each constant-drive ramp reaches the same tripwire force at a different time after touch. The slower approach delays force accumulation.

steps.title: Charge response after the fast crossing

steps.title: Create more time with a guarded approach
steps.description: At the lower speed, the same contact-loop response leaves a longer interval before the ramp reaches the latch limit. This is a timing margin under the stipulated ramp model.

steps.title: Keep onset separate from stopping
steps.description: Crossing the limit line is unacceptable in this counterfactual ramp. The diagram does not describe how force actually changes after braking starts.

title: Phase plane of the shoulder swing

scope: This phase plane plots path speed against position, not speed against time. The result uses the chapter’s stipulated acceleration, torque, and velocity limits.

steps.title: Use the tightest acceleration bound

steps.title: Switch before reaching the speed ceiling
steps.description: The rest-to-rest move changes from acceleration to braking at the marked switch point below the joint velocity limit.

steps.title: Remain inside the feasible envelope
steps.description: The braking branch returns path speed to zero at the final position. The jerk-limited profile stays inside the bang-bang envelope to avoid an instantaneous torque step.

steps.title: Read the duration tradeoff
steps.description: The legend reports a longer duration for jerk limiting under these bounds. This is a declared constrained-move comparison, not an architecture-wide overhead percentage.

title: Where each candidate placement runs

supply.label: Battery, DRAM, and isolated rail dependencies

steps.title: Retain the common-cause accounting

title: Three reference events, three bounds

events.label: Appearance, capture, dispatch, and last renewal

steps.title: Choose the true reference event
steps.description: Appearance, sensor capture, dispatch, and last valid renewal occur at different times. A bound begins at its named event, not wherever logging is convenient.

steps.title: Expose the missing admission interval
steps.description: The hatched dispatch-to-admission segment is drawn at the ceiling that spends the spare, not as an observed duration. It is outside the capture subtotal.

steps.title: Score the stalled proposer from renewal

steps.title: Do not substitute the capture subtotal
steps.description: The capture-based subtotal adds evidence age but omits dispatch-to-admission. Its larger number is not a complete appearance-to-stop bound.

steps.title: Leave unavailable evidence unavailable
steps.description: Appearance-to-capture is also unwitnessed. Without that interval and admission delay, an appearance-referenced guarantee has no established value.

title: The machine under test and its witnesses
question: How can fault containment be judged independently of the controller being tested?
scope: This is the declared test architecture and fault placement. The hold-up duration label uses the chapter’s optimistic all-weight screen, not a completed qualification result.

proposer.label: F1 proposer and F2 camera faults

controller.label: Safety MCU and F4b rail feed

drive.label: F3 fieldbus and F4a drive supply

steps.title: Inject at named physical interfaces
steps.description: F1 disrupts the proposer and F2 the camera link. These faults test different dependencies and must not be conflated into a single software error.

steps.title: Stress the permission and actuation chain
steps.description: F3 targets fieldbus delivery, while F4a and F4b target different supplies. The permission rail’s hold-up must outlast the required flag-to-brakes response under the qualified load.

steps.title: Observe the physical result
steps.description: The loaded base is where torque becomes motion. Containment must be judged against the declared physical outcome, not only a controller log message.

steps.title: Keep the oracle independent
steps.description: The reference clock, logic analyzer, bus sniffer, current probes, encoders, camera, and rail digitizer provide witness measurements on independent clock and supply paths.

title: One F1 trace against its oracle
question: Can a stop pass its distance check while failing its onset deadline?
scope: These are model timelines, not measured traces. The oracle requires both independently witnessed timing and travel predicates.

lease.label: Proposer termination, lease expiry, and rejected probe

margins.label: Rest times and signed distance margins

steps.title: Anchor to the last valid renewal
steps.description: The proposer task is killed after the final renewal. Lease expiry remains tied to that valid renewal; the later probe is refused rather than extending authority.

steps.title: Witness each response stage
steps.description: The permission tick issues the stop, and the fieldbus delivers the frame. Neither event alone proves powered deceleration has started.

steps.title: Score onset independently
steps.description: The dashed powered-deceleration trace begins after the onset bound. That gives a negative timing margin even if the machine eventually stops.

steps.title: Retain the distance result without excusing lateness
steps.description: The lower curves integrate to travel, and the late curve can retain a small nonnegative distance margin. The timing failure still makes the combined oracle fail.

title: Camera ray frustum lifting and BEV splatting
question: Why does lifting camera features into BEV not establish collision clearance?
scope: Learned depth hypotheses remain uncertain. A shared metric coordinate frame is not a validated metric error bound.

steps.title: Extract a feature at a pixel
steps.description: The first panel maps image location to a learned feature vector. The feature has not yet become a unique metric obstacle location.

steps.title: Spread evidence over depth hypotheses
steps.description: The lifting panel weights candidate depths along the camera ray. Monocular ambiguity remains even though each hypothesis has a metric coordinate.

steps.title: Accumulate in a common frame
steps.description: Extrinsics place contributions into shared BEV cells. Summation combines evidence; it does not certify distance accuracy.

steps.title: Add the validated clearance allowance
steps.description: The last panel distinguishes estimated depth from the checked inset. Metric residuals, bias, and a justified error bound must be established before permission relies on clearance.

title: Gaussian memory and clearance handoff
question: When is Gaussian scene memory suitable for collision checking?
scope: Novel-view quality is visual evidence, not a conservative distance guarantee. Geometry conversion and its error bound require separate validation.

steps.title: Track the observation pose
steps.description: RGB-D input and pose tracking locate incoming observations relative to scene memory. Pose uncertainty remains relevant to any later geometry claim.

steps.title: Update a Gaussian representation
steps.description: Means, covariance, opacity, and appearance parameters represent the scene for rendering. Adaptive density control splits, clones, or prunes representation elements.

steps.title: Separate rendering from clearance
steps.description: The upper branch rasterizes novel views. The lower branch is only candidate occupancy or distance until conversion error is bounded and clearance is checked.

title: Constructed spatial-memory storage scenarios
question: What assumptions make spatial-memory representations scale differently?
scope: Constructed storage models, not equal-fidelity or measured-runtime benchmarks. Fixed Gaussian count need not meet stricter geometry targets as resolution increases.

axes.label: Grid resolution and logarithmic storage axes

steps.title: Read the allocation assumptions
steps.description: The legend declares bytes per dense voxel, bytes per assumed surface cell, and a fixed Gaussian count and packing. These are different representation assumptions.

steps.title: Allocate the whole volume
steps.description: The dense cube’s cubic scaling makes storage rise quickly as grid cells per dimension increase. The plotted points are computed from the declared model.

steps.title: Allocate an assumed surface
steps.description: The surface-cell model grows quadratically under its stipulated allocation. It does not claim every octree scene always has that occupied-cell count.

steps.title: Do not confuse fixed count with fixed fidelity
steps.description: The flat Gaussian line holds primitive count constant while grid resolution varies. A stricter geometry requirement can demand more Gaussians, so this is not a quality-matched victory.

title: Probabilistic octree volumetric mapping
question: What does raycasting add beyond accumulated point returns?
scope: The three panels illustrate a historical mapping pipeline. A displayed map is not by itself a guarantee that every free cell is currently observed.

steps.title: Start with surface returns
steps.description: The raw point cloud records sampled surfaces seen along the traversal. Missing returns alone do not label every unsampled location as free.

steps.title: Represent occupancy volumetrically
steps.description: The middle panel places occupied evidence in volumetric cells. Probabilistic updates can combine repeated, uncertain observations.

steps.title: Record evidence of emptiness
steps.description: Raycasting also updates cells traversed by sensor rays before a return. Explicit free, occupied, and unknown space lets memory retire a phantom obstacle when new evidence supports it.

title: Diffusion policy architecture
question: Which parts of diffusion policy generation are proposals, and which path admits physical action?
scope: Diffusion iterations are inference evaluations, not physical time steps. A generated or sent prefix is still a proposal until permission admits it.

steps.title: Condition on recent observations
steps.description: Camera images and robot state are encoded into a conditioning history. The history shapes the generated proposal rather than bypassing admission.

steps.title: Generate a multi-step candidate
steps.description: Sequential noise-network evaluations refine a noisy chunk. The resulting horizon contains proposed future action steps, distinct from the denoising computation count.

steps.title: Send only the prefix
steps.description: The execution prefix is sent while the unexecuted tail is discarded before replanning. Committing fewer steps permits later observations to influence a new proposal.

steps.title: Admit commands independently
steps.description: The prefix crosses the proposal boundary into the permission path. Only admitted commands reach the drives and can become physical work.

title: Diffusion policy action chunk denoising and receding-horizon decoupling
question: How do alternative action modes, denoising, and dual-rate dispatch fit together?
scope: The image is a schematic. Candidate paths still require clearance checks; the board link connects processors with distinct memories.

steps.title: Avoid averaging incompatible routes
steps.description: The direct-regression mean passes through the obstacle between two demonstrated modes. Conditional sampling can select an alternative mode, although it does not certify clearance.

steps.title: Refine in inference time
steps.description: The center column goes from noise through a coarse candidate to an action chunk. These refinement stages do not depict the robot physically executing the noisy paths.

steps.title: Transfer across processor boundaries
steps.description: The asynchronous application sampler sends the chunk with CRC and sequence information over the black-channel link. It does not write shared MCU memory.

steps.title: Check before physical dispatch
steps.description: The safety MCU owns active and filling buffers and runs freshness, spline, and slew checks on its fast tick. Only the admitted command proceeds to the drives.
